behaviours.excerpt: The current draft meets Halcyon’s requirements, including customer access to per-model test results and a 36-month minimum lead time for built-in suppression.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, property damage, or emergency shut-off to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a preliminary account and known impacts. Other thermal incidents must be reported within 5 business days. Affected customers must be notified directly within 24 hours for an incident presenting an imminent safety risk, and within 5 business days for other reportable incidents.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% per model. A model exceeding that limit must be reported to the regulator within 30 days with a corrective-action plan and retested within 12 months. Full per-model results must be provided to the regulator and to customers who own or are considering that model; individual-company per-model failure rates need not be published to the general public.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new home battery models must include remote emergency shut-off capability for units manufactured 18 months after adoption of this standard. For units already installed, manufacturers must offer and complete a compatible retrofit, or an equivalent regulator-approved safety measure, within 6 years of adoption.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: Built-in fire suppression is required on new home battery units manufactured 3 years after adoption of this standard. The system must be validated for the battery chemistry and installation environment under a regulator-approved protocol.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A recall is mandatory when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; the manufacturer must notify the regulator and affected customers within 24 hours of confirming the threshold is exceeded and promptly implement the regulator-approved recall.

document.section_notes: The final text is a complete, signed agreement that keeps the 8-per-100,000 model-specific recall trigger with no transition, which directly exposes Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9). The S2 limit is 5% with per-model results given to regulators and customers but not published, and the S3 retrofit deadline sits at 6 years, which favours Northwind's 38% shut-off coverage. The new-unit shut-off deadline of 18 months falls outside the ≤12-month acceptable range, so S3 is rated weakened on the exact parameter rules.
